findings.issue: SEC-5's absolute wording that the logging path 'cannot leak a secret' rests on the producer invariant for ArrProviderError.Message (and, transitively, WorkProcessingResult.Reason and MediaMatch.AmbiguityReason) rather than on boundary redaction: those fields are length-bounded/trimmed but not control-character-stripped. All current producers were re-verified as fixed, code-owned strings (no URL, key, header, or provider response text), so the claim holds and CR/LF log-forging is not exploitable today. This is a future-regression risk only.

findings.issue: Configuration validation accepts an absolute http/https base URL without rejecting embedded user information. ArrTags' own connection identity (ArrConnectionId) derives only scheme/host/port/path and excludes userinfo and the API key, and ArrTags never logs the request URI, so the plugin's instrumented call sites cannot emit a URL credential. However, if an administrator embedded credentials in the base URL, framework-level HttpClient logging (host category, not gated by LogVerbosity) could include them in the request URI. This is pre-existing (not introduced by Goal F), requires admin misconfiguration, and is outside the instrumented logging call sites.
findings.description: Base-URL userinfo is not rejected by config validation; ArrTags' own identity/logging excludes it, but framework HttpClient logging could include it. Pre-existing and out of the Goal F call-site scope.

sec5_assessment: The rewritten SEC-5 (docs/limitations.md:509-547) accurately and completely states the shipped redaction contract and is consistent with ADR-020. It records: (1) ArrTags logs through the host ILogger<T>/ILoggerFactory pipeline (clause 1); (2) at the bounded, validated, secret-free LogVerbosity (Off/Error/Warning/Information/Debug/Trace, default Warning) read from the current configuration snapshot and applied without restart (clauses 2-3); (3) every log call emits only bounded, already-redacted values per the clause 4 allowlist (ArrProviderError code/retryability/message, non-secret connection identity, configuration version, bounded reason codes/enums, item/record identifiers, counts) and never an API key, webhook secret, SecretLease value, X-Api-Key/X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header, raw request/response body, full provider payload, or mutable PluginConfiguration; (4) the emitted data shape is identical at every verbosity level, so raising verbosity cannot expand a redacted value; (5) volume is bounded by the code-owned LogThrottle (clause 6, architecture section 12); (6) verbosity is not output-affecting (clause 5); and (7) the logging path is covered by a dedicated security review (clause 8, this report). The pre-10.2 false assurance ('the plugin has no logging call sites, so no plugin log path can leak a secret') is gone from every named document (grep-verified; remaining matches are intentional historical/work-description references in ADR-020 Context, PLANS.md, and the changelog). SEC-5 and SEC-9 are mutually consistent: both plugin-initiated outbound surfaces are bounded and secret-free, neither expands with verbosity, SEC-9 remains the only administrator-visible notification, and logging is a diagnostic mechanism (clause 7). One nuance, recorded as SEC-10.3-1, is that SEC-5's absolute 'cannot leak a secret' wording depends on the ArrProviderError.Message producer invariant rather than boundary redaction; all current producers were re-verified as fixed code-owned strings, so the statement holds for the shipped code. The named companion documents (architecture sections 11 and 12, data-model 3.12, README) were also checked and match the implementation, and the stale 'durations' wording was corrected.
accepted_limitations: The ArrProviderError.Message (and transitive WorkProcessingResult.Reason / MediaMatch.AmbiguityReason) redaction depends on the code-owned producer invariant; the fields are length-bounded but not control-character-stripped. All current producers are fixed strings, so this is a future-regression risk only and is tracked in docs/implementation/10.2/security-review.json. No docs/limitations.md entry is strictly required.

summary: Task 10.3's documentation rewrite and the current HEAD logging path pass the independent security review. The rewritten docs/limitations.md SEC-5 accurately and completely states the ADR-020 redaction contract (bounded secret-free LogVerbosity, the clause 4 allowlist and the explicit never-emitted values, identical data shape at every level, code-owned LogThrottle volume bound, verbosity not output-affecting, and the dedicated security review), and it no longer carries the false 'no logging call sites' assurance; SEC-5 and SEC-9 are consistent. The implementation is unchanged since commit 8407964, and a fresh spot-check of all 21 instrumented call sites, the facade, the throttle, the DI wiring, and the verbosity gate confirms: no secret-bearing value reaches a log line, no level-conditional payload expansion exists, there is no custom ILoggerProvider/sink and no host ILoggerFactory replacement, and the volume bound holds (5 per category/event per minute, one suppression summary per window rollover, 256-key cap over a code-owned key space). Build is clean (0 warnings/0 errors) and the suite is Failed 0, Passed 1363, Skipped 63, Total 1426 with the 65-case LogRedactionTests all passing. There are 0 open BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM findings. Two LOW documentation/defense-in-depth residuals are recorded (the ArrProviderError.Message producer invariant, already tracked in the 10.2 review; and the stale docs/planning/v1.1.md current-state line), plus two INFORMATIONAL observations (live host sink verification deferred to task 14.3; pre-existing base-URL userinfo validation gap). None blocks Gate 10's security criterion, which requires the review recorded with no open BLOCKER/HIGH. Verdict: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS.
